dev_notes: src/compose.mjs holds the model: composeTargets, needsNote, inputsOf (the entry at the last edition, now, and its events' what and why — not why_from, so vouching for a reason changes nothing), composeReportFor, composeLine, stamped and ordered. src/commands/compose.mjs is the brief and `compose complete`; TASKS.compose in src/prompt.mjs checks the report after an agent runs. Compositions live in .ledger/compositions.json, one per release, with `changes` (id → bullets), `summary` (id → the first page's sentence for that entry; older editions carry `new`/`changed`/`in_place` lists of { text, covers } and `quiet` instead, and may carry `matters` and `message`, which nothing reads and prepare complete refuses in an open release), and the stamp (`date`, `commit`, `inputs`, `verified`). The store hands each feature its composed bullets, and for the open release before anything is composed, its events as a draft (`changes_draft`). LedgerHtml.summaryHtml in src/render/ledger-html.mjs prints one line per moved entry from `summary`, in the order changedSection prints them, linking to id="f-<id>" (an older composition's items print with all their numbers), falls back to entry names when a composition has nothing for the first page, and adds a draft note when the open release's composition isn't up to date. messageFor in src/compose.mjs builds the message from the overview and `summary`, under the first page's headings; nothing writes it.

history.name: Preparing an edition
history.description: The command ledger prepare prints a brief for an agent session that writes the overview, a sentence per feature for the first page, and a note on each changed entry. The agent also records unrecorded work, asks you missing reasons, and checks its text against the code.
history.how_to_see: Run ledger prepare: it says what the release holds, then prints the brief to paste into your agent session. When the agent is done, ledger prepare complete prints the first page's lists and the message as the edition will.
